title: Glasgow's giant Commonwealth Games Nessie has surfaced in an unexpected new home
excerpt: The fate of a prop from Glasgow's 2026 Commonwealth Games Opening Ceremony has been revealed after it was sold at auction.
content:
The fate of a prop from Glasgow's 2026 Commonwealth Games Opening Ceremony has been revealed after it sold for thousands at auction.

The massive Nessie, which shared the stage with Outlander's Sam Heughan, sold for £2,400 last month, with its new owner remaining a mystery.

That is, until now, as officials have revealed that the impressive depiction of the Loch Ness Monster has touched down in Valley View at Goulding's an adventure park in South Lanarkshire.

Read more

A statement on the park's Facebook page said: "We've had some unusual deliveries recently, but this one might just top them all!

"Meet Nessie, the huge Loch Ness Monster who starred in the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games Opening Ceremony… and she's now made her way to the Clyde Valley!

"Why is she here? You'll have to wait and see…

"Nessie will surface at a very special Valley View event soon! Follow us and keep an eye on valleyviewatgouldings.com for the big reveal."

Nessie isn't the only prop to have raised the hands of bidders.

We previously reported that the giant Tunnock's teacake, which itself weighs a tonne, sold for £700 when it went under the hammer.

(Image: Andrew Milligan)

Other items sold include a sparkling traffic cone, a nod to Glasgow's famous Duke of Wellington statue, which went for £320, as well as a signed ball from the final of the netball competition which brought in £300.
